analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines 2492-2512 per the patch). It adds prose on Flint constrained-decode chaining (FlintNativeProtocolConstraint and FlintAnswerStopConstraint, maskCacheKey, device-mask caching), the automatic paged list entry for RecursiveSI/flint-int4 at legacy serving width on M5 Pro/Max/Ultra, and fused decode kernels (qkv, gate+up, MoE combine). No code, wire protocol, attestation, key handling, or authorization is modified in the supplied evidence, so no regression is demonstrable.

The prose makes security-relevant claims that I could not verify without the source: (1) chained constrained decode gives a token stream identical to unchained decode, with redraw from retained logits that restores penalty state and per-row RNG step; (2) the device mask cache is keyed by constraint state and not per-request or per-tenant data; (3) the answer-stop and tool-boundary constraints still withhold reasoning and stop text under chaining; (4) byte-identical outputs from fused kernels. If the underlying code diverges, T-007 (output integrity) and TB-007 isolation (T-028 residual data) could be affected. A shared cached mask keyed only by state holds no prompt content, so it is unlikely to add a cross-tenant channel. The mask cache and speculative chaining could add timing differences, but T-041/SEC-035 covers the TTFT oracle for prefix caching and this is a different mechanism. The prefix-cache scope, KEK, HMAC naming and TTL controls in T-041 are not touched by this diff. Unit 9bceb6d953b336e2:8 is base text (lines 2366-2568) and 9bceb6d953b336e2:9 is head text (lines 1-415, with no changed lines). Neither shows any security-affecting change. The accompanying source changes, if any exist in this PR, need their own review.
